concepts.def: The democratic republic set up after 1918, with a constitution agreed at Weimar in 1919 featuring proportional representation and Article 48 emergency powers.
After the French occupation of the Ruhr, the government printed money until the mark became worthless, wiping out savings before the Rentenmark restored stability.
Hitler's failed armed takeover in Bavaria; his trial publicity and prison time writing Mein Kampf led him to switch to winning power through elections.
Depression unemployment of around six million by 1932 fuelled Nazi electoral success, and backstairs intrigue made Hitler Chancellor in January 1933.
Passed after the Reichstag Fire, the Act let Hitler's government make laws without the Reichstag, providing the legal foundation of the dictatorship.
The SS and Gestapo, Goebbels's propaganda, and the Night of the Long Knives in 1934 secured Hitler's position as Führer after Hindenburg's death.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Germany: Development of Dictatorship 1918-45 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Germany: Development of Dictatorship 1918-45 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Germany: Development of Dictatorship 1918-45.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which law allowed Hitler to make laws without the Reichstag?
options: The Enabling Act of 1933
The Treaty of Versailles
The Dawes Plan
The Nuremberg Laws

mcqs.q: What was the immediate context of the 1923 hyperinflation crisis?
options: The government printed money during the French occupation of the Ruhr
The Wall Street Crash destroyed German banks
Allied bombing wrecked German industry
The cost of building the autobahns

mcqs.q: Who were the main victims of the Night of the Long Knives in 1934?
options: Ernst Röhm and the SA leadership, along with other rivals of Hitler
The leaders of the Communist Party only
Senior army generals
Members of the Hitler Youth

mcqs.q: When did Hitler become Chancellor of Germany?
options: January 1933
November 1923
October 1929
August 1934

mcqs.q: Did Hitler seize power in a violent coup in 1933?
options: No - he was legally appointed Chancellor in January 1933 through a deal brokered with President Hindenburg, then dismantled democracy from inside using the Reichstag Fire Decree and Enabling Act.
The Nazis won every German election after 1920.
Hitler became Chancellor by winning a national referendum.
Hitler took power by leading a successful armed revolution in 1933.

mcqs.q: Did the Nazis ever win a majority in a free election?
options: Hyperinflation was caused by Hitler to destroy the Weimar Republic.
Most Germans voted the Nazis into power with a clear majority.
No - their best result in a fully free election was about 37 per cent in July 1932; they never won an overall majority while elections remained free.
The Nazis won every German election after 1920.

mcqs.q: Did the 1923 hyperinflation directly bring Hitler to power?
options: Hyperinflation in 1923 led immediately to Hitler taking over Germany.
The Nazis won every German election after 1920.
No - the Stresemann era restored stability after 1924, and it was the Depression from 1929 that revived Nazi fortunes; Hitler only became Chancellor in 1933.
Hyperinflation was caused by Hitler to destroy the Weimar Republic.
